objective: Eliminate all three enemy Marines within 60 decisions. Apply this policy independently each episode: concentrate fire for an early kill, preserve firing strength, then finish promptly.
opening: Advance together toward the central search location using legal endpoints that reduce search distance without separating from teammates. The enemy initially waits, then attack-moves toward the allied spawn; meet it with all three Marines supporting each other. On contact, stop advancing units already able to fire and bring lagging Marines into range.
target_selection: Use a shared target ranking: first enemies legally attackable and currently in range of at least two allies; then lowest health plus shields, greatest ready-in-range allied coverage, shortest distance to the allied centroid, and lowest enemy index. If none has two-unit coverage, prioritize greatest in-range coverage before health. Maintain focus while the target remains competitive. A Marine unable to attack the shared target should shoot its highest-ranked in-range legal alternative, or approach the shared target if no immediate shot exists. Do not assume another ally's pending attack will finish a target.
movement_and_cooldowns: When ready with a legal in-range target, normally attack. During cooldown, repeat the attack unless retreat offers a clear survival benefit; movement can sacrifice the next shot, especially when cooldown is at most the 8-loop decision interval. For a threatened Marine, select a legal endpoint increasing distance from nearby enemies while retaining teammate support; break ties by proximity to the allied centroid, then action ID. Reassess after one interval. Attack availability within distance 6 does not prove firing range; use range relations. Stop cancels orders and is not a waiting action.
priorities: Remove one enemy quickly; keep healthy Marines firing while a damaged teammate withdraws.
Avoid whole-team retreat, isolated pursuit, and repeated movement that prevents firing.
As time runs short, prioritize closing distance and damage over prolonged preservation.
contingencies: If several allies take damage, designate only one retreat candidate: lowest health fraction among recently damaged allies, then greatest recent damage, then lowest ally index. Retreat only when the endpoint improves survival; others sustain fire.
If visibility is lost, regroup and search toward last observed contact, then the central corridor and enemy spawn prior. Unseen enemies remain unknown.
If an action is rejected or expected progress fails, recheck current legal choices and observations. Acceptance alone does not establish firing.
assumptions: Combat occurs on one flat walkable rectangle, x in [2,30), y in [7,25); there is no terrain choke or height advantage.
Spawn anchors and opponent behavior are priors. Current observations govern positions, health, range, and readiness.

unit_roles.guidance: Every Marine supplies focused ranged damage. Healthy units maintain contact; the selected wounded unit briefly yields ground and resumes firing when safe. No abilities or healing are available.
